papers.title: Integrating wavelet signal processing and machine learning for EEG-based detection of brain diseases with representative channel selection.
papers.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
papers.summary: Proposed an integrated wavelet signal processing and machine learning framework using Discrete Wavelet Packet Transform features (approximate entropy, rhythm energy ratio, C0-complexity, zero-crossing rate) with representative single-channel selection. Single-channel detection accuracies reached 84.52% (F4) for schizophrenia, 86.54% (F4) for Parkinson's disease, and 93.10% (Fp1) for depression.

papers.title: Repeated self-administered EEG recordings enable longitudinal measurement of brain activity at home
papers.summary: Five participants completed repeated self-administered four-channel consumer EEG recordings at home during rest and an auditory oddball task with and without cognitive load, capturing alpha increases with eye closure, load-related theta changes, and clear event-related responses. Aggregating sessions improved reliability, with split-half reliability of the N1-like response rising from r = .22 for one session to r = .76 for seven sessions per half.

papers.title: Simulation-based neural dynamics of stress-related negative cognitive bias in depressive symptoms: a dynamical EEG/ERP framework.
papers.summary: Developed a simulation-based nonlinear state-space framework with three states (negative bias, cognitive control, arousal) linking stress-related negative cognitive bias to EEG/ERP measures, testing it on 180 simulated participants. The pre-specified quartic model achieved mean held-out RMSE 0.060 versus 0.436 for an interaction-only candidate, and state-reconstruction RMSE rose from 0.152 to 0.232 under 15% loading perturbations; these are model-sensitivity results, not clinical effect estimates.

papers.title: Correction: The PREP pipeline: standardized preprocessing for large-scale EEG analysis.
papers.summary: Published erratum correcting the article 'The PREP pipeline: standardized preprocessing for large-scale EEG analysis' (DOI: 10.3389/fninf.2015.00016), with no new findings reported.

papers.title: Next generation Human Neocortical Neurosolver model with biophysically realistic somatic, dendritic and synaptic dynamics
papers.summary: Presents a substantially updated Human Neocortical Neurosolver canonical circuit model with electrophysiological and synaptic properties tuned to human tissue, adding L5 ET dendritic Ca2+ spikes and shorter L2/3 dendritic spikes. Demonstrates workflows for disentangling somatic, synaptic, and dendritic contributions to human EEG/MEG event-related responses and oscillations.

papers.title: Cross-cohort validation of EEG biomarkers using a pre-registered three-criterion framework: a demonstration in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
papers.summary: Applied a pre-registered three-criterion framework (cross-sectional discrimination, within-subject reliability, cross-cohort effect consistency) to screen 18 EEG features for ALS biomarkers across three independent cohorts. Gamma power, theta power, and spectral entropy met all criteria, while cross-cohort reliability differences (e.g., relative beta power ICC 0.09 vs 0.93) were large relative to disease-associated signal and bootstrap analyses showed selected-set sensitivity to sample composition.

papers.title: Theoretical analysis of transfer learning for temporally dependent observations.
papers.journal: Bernoulli : official journal of the Bernoulli Society for Mathematical Statistics and Probability
papers.summary: Proposed a two-step transfer learning procedure for high-dimensional vector autoregressive models with temporally dependent observations, including auxiliary-set selection and debiasing techniques for parameter inference and confidence intervals. Under mild conditions allowing heavy tails and dependence, the method attains the minimax rate, with empirical validation on simulated data and an EEG dataset.

papers.title: Resting-state EEG spectral characteristics before and after a single auditory integration training session in children with autism spectrum disorder.
papers.summary: Examined resting-state EEG spectral characteristics in 20 children with ASD and 15 typically developing children, and pre-post changes around a single 30-min Berard auditory integration training session using FOOOF spectral parameterization. ASD showed higher delta and lower theta/alpha/beta relative power at baseline; post-session delta decreased and beta/gamma increased, but aperiodic exponent and offset showed no significant changes.

papers.title: TARS-EEG: a tropical algebraic representation for EEG seizure detection.
papers.summary: Introduces TARS-EEG, an interpretable tropical algebraic representation that maps short EEG segments into multiscale max-plus and min-plus dilation, erosion, gradient, and residue profiles with a Tropical Seizure Index for seizure detection. Under recording-group-aware five-fold cross-validation, MLP reached 97.70% mean accuracy and XGBoost a ROC-AUC of 0.9926, outperforming individual neighbourhood-scale representations.

papers.title: Sequential syntax of EEG microstates captures the temporal dynamics of inhibitory control.
papers.summary: Applied a sequence-based framework combining conditional successor analysis with multiple sequence alignment to EEG microstate sequences from 30 healthy adults during a Go/NoGo task. Conditional successor analysis identified three NoGo-early motifs (A-C-D, B-A-D, E-A-D) passing through microstate A and ending in D, while sequence alignment showed non-random temporal organization across all conditions.

papers.title: Automatic classification of seizure adequacy in electroconvulsive therapy: A proof-of-concept study
papers.summary: Using 1000 ECT session EEGs from 130 patients labeled by experts into null-response, threshold, and adequate seizure quality categories, the authors trained machine learning classifiers on raw EEG and achieved AUC >0.9 for 0 vs. threshold and threshold vs. adequate discrimination, though prediction of seizure quality in subsequent treatments was only moderate. Adding clinical variables did not improve performance.

papers.title: Source-resolved electroencephalogram microstates reveal opposing prefrontal-posterior dynamics and a candidate temporal-to-precuneus pathway in disorders of consciousness.
papers.summary: In high-density EEG from 33 disorders-of-consciousness patients and 19 controls, source-localized microstate analysis revealed opposing dynamics: right prefrontal microstate 3 was enhanced in vegetative state/unresponsive wakefulness syndrome while parieto-occipital-temporal microstate 4 was higher in minimally conscious state, with microstate 4 occurrence discriminating the groups (AUC = 0.812). Hypothesis-generating Granger causality nominally implicated stronger right middle temporal-to-precuneus flow in minimally conscious state, though this did not survive network-level correction.

papers.title: Robust Feature Engineering Techniques for Designing Efficient Motor Imagery-Based Systems Using Multidomain Electroencephalography
papers.summary: Extracted 416 time-, frequency-, and wavelet-domain features from 16-channel EEG in the MILimbEEG dataset and used MRMR to select four features for SVM, KNN, Naive Bayes, and decision tree classifiers with 10-fold cross-validation. Gaussian-kernel SVM achieved the highest testing accuracies of 92.50% for motor activities and 95.48% for motor imagery, with precision/recall/F1 of 86.97%/88.33%/87.04% for motor imagery.

papers.title: A Dual-Branch Graph and Convolutional Network for Interpretable Movement EEG Classification
papers.summary: Proposes a dual-branch EEG decoder combining an LGGNet-inspired local-global graph branch with an EEGNet-style convolutional branch for movement-versus-rest classification, achieving a mean F1-score of 0.74 ± 0.06 in leave-one-subject-out cross-validation on the Ofner upper-limb dataset. Learned graph connectivity was consistently strongest in the left parietal low region (P1/P3), opposite the performed right-arm movements, yielding an anatomically interpretable representation.

papers.title: Cue modality modulates dynamic functional network organization during motor imagery: Evidence from EEG functional connectivity and spatiotemporal decoding.
papers.summary: Combined phase-locking-value functional connectivity analysis with a CNN-TemporalConv-MLP spatiotemporal decoding model to test how cue modality (visual vs auditory) and imagery type (kinesthetic vs visual) shape post-cue motor imagery EEG networks. Cue-modality effects were frequency- and time-specific (higher theta PLV and early beta PLV with visual cues, later beta PLV with auditory cues), and PLV features decoded cue modality moderately well, with imagery-type decoding improving when cue background was held constant.

papers.title: EEG and hedonic responses to sonic-seasoning soundscapes: a dataset.
papers.summary: Releases an open dataset of 14-channel EMOTIV EPOC X EEG (128 Hz) from 30 adults exposed to two contrasting soundscapes, with synchronized event markers, resting calibration, per-soundscape liking ratings, stimulus audio files, and demographics. The data add a neurophysiological measurement angle to sonic-seasoning and multisensory marketing research, released as recorded with contact- and signal-quality indices retained for re-users.

papers.title: Predicting Motor Recovery in the Subacute Phase of Stroke: The Role of Passive Motor Task and Electroencephalogram Brain Networks.
papers.summary: Compared passive robotic movement, active execution, motor imagery, and No-Go tasks as EEG-based prognostic predictors in 10 subacute stroke patients across two time points; the passive task model gave the strongest internal prediction (RMSE 5.94, nested LOSO CV-R2 0.91). Consistent prognostic features were ipsilesional/contralesional motor-area event-related desynchronization, characteristic path length, and clustering coefficient, with less overactivation and hyperconnectivity in the early subacute phase.

papers.title: Characteristics of EEG Microstate Analysis of Power Grip and Precision Grip Hand Movements from Motor Planning to Execution.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.summary: Used high-density EEG microstate analysis to compare precision grip and power grip across motor planning and execution in 24 healthy participants. Planning microstate sequences were identical for both grips but the fourth ERP microstate was longer in precision grip, while execution showed stronger MSC suppression, greater MSD activation, and distinct transition probabilities in precision grip, with Random Forest reaching 72.07% for precision grip versus rest.

papers.title: Beyond Onset Timing: Longer Sound Envelope Duration Enhances Neural Representation of the Musical Beat.
papers.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
papers.summary: EEG in participants listening to rhythmic sequences showed that longer sound envelope duration enhanced neural beat periodicity even though this periodicity was not prominent in the acoustic envelope or a biomimetic auditory nerve model, indicating higher-level processing beyond onset timing. The results support a holistic account in which features beyond onset timing contribute to the internal representation of musical beat.

papers.title: Combined MEG and EEG suggest a limbic source network for the P3.
papers.summary: Re-evaluated P3 sources using combined MEG and EEG with MRI-based noise-normalized minimum-norm source analysis whose cortical source space included the hippocampal cornu ammonis. At the P3 peak, source analysis showed strong retrosplenial cortex and weaker hippocampal sources, with later insula and anterior mid-cingulate activity, supporting a limbic-system interpretation of the P3; simulations indicated combined MEG/EEG improved source specificity.

papers.title: Cortical Network Alterations and Treatment-Induced Reorganization in Panic Disorder: A Longitudinal High-Density EEG Study.
papers.summary: In a longitudinal high-density EEG study, drug-naïve panic disorder patients showed frequency-specific cortical network disruptions (enhanced α-band connectivity within/between default mode, frontoparietal, and dorsal attention networks; reduced θ/δ connectivity) with 86.32% SVM classification accuracy versus controls, and these network features reorganized after 6 weeks of venlafaxine treatment alongside clinical improvement.

papers.title: Electrophysiology of multisite direct electrical stimulation in the human brain
papers.summary: Using stereo-EEG in 20 participants, this study characterized electrophysiological responses to simultaneous multisite direct electrical stimulation, finding that dual-site stimulation engaged larger networks than single-site, responses were mostly explained by linear superposition but included sublinear (proximal) and supralinear (network-connected late) nonlinearities, and low-intensity dual-site stimulation matched or exceeded higher-intensity single-site stimulation.

papers.title: Brain-computer interfaces for neurodegenerative diseases: A comprehensive review of closed-loop systems from diagnosis to neural rehabilitation.
papers.summary: This comprehensive review analyzes brain-computer interface (BCI) development and closed-loop systems for neurodegenerative diseases, focusing on applications in Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis for early diagnosis, functional reconstruction, and neuromodulation, and discusses technical, clinical translation, and ethical challenges plus future directions such as multimodal fusion and adaptive algorithms.

papers.title: Nogo-related frontal theta-band activity after magnetic seizure therapy in treatment-resistant depression: an exploratory task-based EEG study.
papers.summary: In an open-label, single-arm trial, 19 patients with treatment-resistant depression received 6-12 sessions of 100-Hz magnetic seizure therapy, with significant symptom reductions (HAMD-24 40.53 to 22.53; MADRS 35.68 to 20.68) and response rates of 42.1-57.9%. Nogo-related frontal theta-band activity at Fz/FCz was lower post-treatment only at an uncorrected threshold and did not survive FDR correction.

papers.title: A unified fixed-wavelet transformer decodes eight EEG classes across motor imagery, P300, and SSVEP paradigms.
papers.summary: The authors developed a unified fixed-wavelet Transformer (Analformer) that decoded eight EEG classes across motor imagery, P300, and SSVEP paradigms in 54 participants, achieving 71.00% mean accuracy after participant-specific fine-tuning, outperforming EEG-Conformer (54.53%), EEGNet (52.30%), and ShallowConvNet (45.35%), with ablation analyses confirming the contributions of fixed wavelets and two-stage training.

papers.title: Non-invasive Temporal Interference Stimulation of the Hippocampus Ameliorates Recognition Memory Impairments in Chronic Restraint Stress Mice.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.summary: In a chronic restraint stress mouse model of depression, 40-Hz temporal interference stimulation targeting the hippocampus improved recognition memory and showed a nonsignificant trend toward improved contextual fear memory, while attenuating hippocampal inhibitory neuron hyperactivation and elevated bilateral DG gamma synchrony. TIS also partially reversed stress-induced synaptic gene expression changes and upregulated GluN2B protein.

papers.title: Neural processing dynamics and social cognition in children with ADHD: a dimensional EEG/ERP approach.
papers.summary: In 61 children (35 with ADHD, 26 controls), this dimensional EEG/ERP study found that poorer theory of mind in ADHD reflected a categorical group difference, whereas ERP indices of emotional-versus-neutral differentiation (amplitude- and latency-reactivity components) predicted parent-reported empathy dimensionally across and within groups, independent of symptom severity.

papers.title: Comparative EEG analysis of Sutra and Tantra meditations: insights into meditative states and long-term traits.
papers.summary: EEG compared long-term Tibetan Buddhist monks practicing Tantra (n=21) versus Sutra (n=20) meditation in a between-groups and within-subjects design, finding the Tantra group had consistently lower alpha power across meditation and baseline conditions. Within subjects, only the Tantra group showed increased individual alpha peak frequency in occipital leads during meditation, decreasing afterward; between-group differences are interpreted as enduring meditative traits.

papers.title: Single-cell dataset of juvenile mouse neurons from the thalamic reticular nucleus: whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology.
papers.summary: The authors release a single-cell whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology dataset from 19 thalamic reticular nucleus interneurons of juvenile (P24–P34) C57Bl/6J mice, covering passive membrane properties, action potential waveform, firing patterns, and rebound-burst dynamics. The resource comprises 18,015 sweeps in NWB format with Parquet indexing and FAIR metadata for computational modeling and machine learning.

papers.title: Effects of heart rate variability biofeedback and relaxation training on ventromedial prefrontal cortex activity in young patients with depressive disorders: An EEG study.
papers.summary: This EEG current source density study compared five weeks of HRV biofeedback versus relaxation training in 45 young patients with depressive disorders, examining bilateral ventromedial prefrontal cortex activity across frequency bands. HRVB produced greater right vmPFC beta3 and left vmPFC high-beta CSD than relaxation training during the transfer stage, while both groups showed increased theta CSD, suggesting HRVB engages vmPFC regulatory processes beyond shared relaxation effects.

papers.title: The Effects of Methylphenidate on the EEG of Children with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder.
papers.summary: This study compared eyes-closed resting EEG in 50 children with ADHD and 50 typically developing children, recording a second EEG 1.5 h after 10 mg methylphenidate in the clinical group. Unmedicated ADHD children showed elevated delta and posterior theta and reduced alpha and gamma activity; methylphenidate increased global absolute and relative beta and relative gamma, though the authors question whether this represents normalization.

papers.title: Sub-Threshold Stochastic Vibration Improves Fingertip Tactile Sensitivity in Stroke Survivors and Healthy Adults, with Source-Localized EEG Evidence for Cortical Network Reorganization in Healthy Adults
papers.summary: In 19 healthy adults and 5 stroke survivors, adding sub-threshold stochastic vibration to a 30 Hz sinusoidal stimulus lowered fingertip detection thresholds in every participant, with sensitivity gains up to 19-fold in healthy adults and 4-fold in stroke survivors. Source-localized 64-channel EEG in healthy adults showed increased functional connectivity, most extensively in the alpha band with frontal involvement, whereas super-threshold noise produced weaker beta-band changes consistent with masking.

papers.title: Disrupted activation of dot perspective task-related EEG generators in forensic patients with borderline personality disorder.
papers.summary: Coupled the dot-perspective task with high-density EEG and inverse source localization to examine neural generators of altercentric and egocentric biases in 24 healthy controls and 14 forensic male BPD patients. In BPD patients no significant differential generator activation was observed for the biases, unlike controls, suggesting reduced mobilization of brain resources when treating Self-Other discrepancy.

papers.title: Disentangling the Spatiotemporal Neural Dynamics of Conflict Detection and Resolution between Lexical and Sublexical Processes in Oral Word Reading: An Intracranial SEEG Study.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: Using intracranial stereo-electroencephalography in 39 participants during Chinese character reading, the study dissociated conflict detection (β activity in fusiform gyrus; θ/α effects across temporal and parietal regions) from inhibitory control (α and β activity in inferior frontal and precentral gyri). Granger causality showed increased β-band connectivity from conflict-processing to inhibitory-control regions under conflict conditions.

papers.title: Multi-level insights into the umami perception of Agrocybe aegerita tripeptides: molecular docking, cell signaling, and electroencephalography.
papers.summary: Five umami tripeptides from Agrocybe aegerita (ENG, PEG, DEL, ECG, DDL) were evaluated via molecular docking, STC-1 cell assays, and electroencephalography. Peptides showed receptor-dependent interactions, biphasic Ca2+ and ATP responses, and modulated cortical δ-band activity, with DDL producing the strongest and most consistent responses.

papers.title: Under-recognized Autoimmune Encephalitis in Patients with Alzheimer's Disease: A Case Series Emphasizing EEG Screening.
papers.summary: A case series of two biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer's disease patients with comorbid autoimmune encephalitis (anti-LGI1 and probable seronegative) reports rapid cognitive decline and argues that routine EEG screening can trigger autoimmune evaluation; immunotherapy and anti-amyloid treatment were associated with cognitive improvement on the MMSE.

papers.title: Design and Test Novel EEG Electrode Attachments for Type 4 Afro-textured Hairstyles
papers.summary: The authors designed and tested 3D-printed hair-anchored EEG electrode attachments for Type 4 Afro-textured hairstyles in 17 healthy adults, comparing them with conventional cap electrodes. Novel attachments reduced electrode-to-scalp distance, gel use, and impedance, decreased disconnection rates from 20% to 0.1%, and improved signal quality without reducing comfort.

papers.title: Institutional Variation in Electroencephalography Utilization in Neonates With Complex Congenital Heart Disease Across the United States and Its Association With Outcomes.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
papers.summary: A retrospective cohort using the Pediatric Health Information System found that only 12.5% of 13,202 neonates with complex congenital heart disease underwent EEG monitoring, with utilization varying from 0% to over 40% across hospitals and rising from ~6% in 2016 to >14% in 2025 while seizure detection among monitored patients increased from 13% to ~26%.

papers.title: Retrieving mangrove biochemical traits under oil pollution using hyperspectral data and transfer learning.
papers.summary: Proposes a teacher-student Multi-Task Convolutional Neural Network with transfer learning and pseudo-labeling to classify mangrove species and retrieve canopy biochemical traits (pigments, sugars, phenols) under oil pollution from airborne and satellite hyperspectral imagery. Reported accuracies exceeded 95% for airborne data, ~70% for PRISMA (5 m), and ~60% for EnMAP (30 m), with spatially consistent biochemical patterns and spectra retaining key absorption features.

papers.title: Macroscopic pulmonary fat embolism following cemented hemiarthroplasty for pathological femoral fracture: A case report with dual-energy CT spectral analysis.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 73-year-old woman with metastatic NSCLC who developed severe hemodynamic instability during cement pressurization for hemiarthroplasty of a pathological proximal femoral lesion, consistent with bone cement implantation syndrome, and recovered with supportive care. Dual-energy CT pulmonary angiography showed a 30 × 15 mm right main pulmonary artery filling defect with mean attenuation of -86.6 HU, progressively more negative CT numbers at lower photon energies, and persistence on virtual noncontrast images, supporting a fatty embolus.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
